note: SPEC vectors, Rust-only. The reference DECLARES `min_privilege` on OperatorMeta and reads it NOWHERE — grep-confirmed: one declaration site, one dataclass field, zero readers, and no `permitted` / `effective_privilege` / `privilege.check` anywhere in the Python engine. So there is nothing to record from it, and these cases are authored from the articles. See conformance/README.md.

cases.name: permitted_admits
cases.why: An owner acting on their own Sustain passes the authorization conjunct, and the call proceeds to the rest of admit().

cases.name: insufficient_tier_names_what_is_missing
cases.why: An observer may not act. The refusal must say the tier HELD and the tier REQUIRED — 'you may not' is useless without which authority was short.

cases.name: no_edge_is_a_different_refusal_from_too_little_authority
cases.why: §IV is explicit that 'you are not a member here' and 'you are a member who may not do this' are different answers. Collapsing them would tell a person to fix the wrong thing.

cases.name: the_weakest_link_along_the_path_governs
cases.why: Permission is the conjunction of every gate on the containing path. Owner of the household and observer on a child gives OBSERVER on the child — nesting can only shrink authority, never widen it.

cases.name: a_missing_edge_anywhere_on_the_path_denies
cases.why: There is no inherit-from-the-parent rule. Owner of the household does not confer membership of a child the principal has no edge to.

cases.name: authorization_is_a_separate_conjunct_from_the_viable_region
cases.why: admit = permitted ∧ guard ∧ result∈A ∧ D. Every conjunct must hold, and each refuses with its OWN rule name so a person can tell 'you may not' from 'your own guard said no' from 'that would break a rule'. ★ The invariant is a CEILING the operator's own guard cannot pre-empt: an authored version using a negative amount was corrected after running it, because `params.amount > 0` fired first and proved the wrong conjunct.

expect.note: authority is decided BEFORE the guard and before the gate, so an unauthorized caller is told they may not act -- not what the state would have done.
the operator's OWN guard, a third distinct conjunct.

cases.name: an_unauthorized_call_leaves_state_byte_unchanged
cases.why: The refusal must produce no mutation, no event and no state change — the same guarantee an enforcement-gate refusal gives, for a different reason.

cases.name: an_unresolved_skin_fails_closed
cases.why: An edge naming a bundle no registry resolves is REFUSED, never quietly demoted to the edge's own tier. A typo'd role name becoming owner-by-accident is exactly what the fail-closed rule prevents.

cases.name: a_skin_may_restrict_an_edge_but_never_widen_it
cases.why: Where both an edge tier and a skin tier are present the WEAKER wins — the same weakest-link algebra as the path walk. A bundle meant to restrict must not be able to widen.
